A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Belief State Transformer research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated proofs and renumbered results.

before.justification: v1 reports original star-graph experiments, TinyStories generation comparisons, ablations and representation probes in Sections 3 and 5, with supporting appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a Fill-in-the-Middle comparison on the star-graph tasks.

M1.justification: The encoders, joint next/previous-token objective, gradient accumulation, and generation/scoring algorithms are unchanged. Appendix E expands the explanation around retained pseudocode; the end-token description clarifies the empty-suffix representation without establishing a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three star-graph configurations and TinyStories, including goal-conditioned and unconditional generation. Adding a comparator to the existing graph tasks does not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Fill-in-the-Middle to the star-graph comparison in Figure 2 and Section 3.4; v1 evaluated it only on TinyStories. The other comparators remain, with Teacherless renamed Multi-token Prediction in the prose.

E3.justification: The new star-graph FIM comparison introduces intermediate-suffix input construction and uniform sampling of suffix lengths (v2 Appendix C.1). Existing experiments retain their data sizes, model configurations, training budgets, metrics and TinyStories judging procedure.

E4.justification: The encoder/objective ablations, beam-search and scoring ablations, representation probes, and illustrative stories are retained. Combining the probing plots into v2 Figure 8 changes presentation, not the analyses performed.

E5.justification: Both versions report binomial confidence intervals and the same six GPT-4 evaluations per story across 100 stories. Existing intervals become graphical error bars; no new repeated-run counts, seed information or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds FIM success rates of approximately 50%, 46% and 16% on G(2,5), G(2,20) and G(5,5), respectively. Existing graph results, TinyStories win rates, ablation outcomes and probing results are retained rather than improved.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix E adds explicit computational cost accounting: GPT training costs O(hn + en^2), BST training O(hn^2 + en^2), and BST inference O(hn + en^2). The belief-state definition, Theorems 1–5 and their proofs otherwise remain unchanged after terminology and appendix renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: compact belief-state learning, success on difficult star graphs, and improved small-scale story generation. The added comparison supports existing claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 extends the shortcut-learning explanation from data augmentation to FIM, arguing that intermediate paths also provide inadequate gradients for learning suitable representations. The existing interpretations of probing and story results, and the small-scale applicability limitations, remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the end token used to represent an empty suffix, documents the new graph FIM input/sampling procedure, and expands training and cost guidance in Appendix E. It also adds a project website link; the PDFs do not establish what resources that website provides. Existing pseudocode and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations for ELMo, BERT, DeepSeek-V3, Momennejad et al. on planning, and Frydenlund on path-star tasks. These broaden context around bidirectional representations, multi-token prediction and planning without fundamentally repositioning the contribution.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, updates publication and affiliation text, introduces BST shorthand, revises terminology and selected paragraphs, and adds acknowledgements and author contributions. The main narrative order remains, while the training appendix receives a limited explanatory expansion.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: v1 Tables 1–3 become v2 Figures 5–7, the two probing figures merge into Figure 8, and new training diagrams appear as Figures 10–11. Figure 2 is redrawn with FIM included. Much of this redisplays existing evidence rather than adding results.

improvement.justification: The added star-graph FIM comparison closes a limited comparison gap, while Appendix E makes training construction and computational costs clearer. Expanded related work also improves context. These provide a modest net gain, although replacing exact TinyStories tables with plots makes numerical lookup harder; the central findings and scalability limitations remain unchanged.
